interpretation: The observational premise of the second horn: the intermediate 'would not change, but now it is always seen to' (νῦν δʼ ἀεὶ φαίνεται). Read as: every state in the domain of the contradictory pair is the start of some change in respect of it. This generalizes Aristotle's appeal to what is seen to every state of the domain, which is the strongest point of the reading and what the formal argument needs; a weaker reading (most states change) would decide only those states.
